What this entry adds is the manifest record the promotion gates key on.

The source lists its functions in REVERSE of ROM order (highest address first) and the file header forbids reordering; with ROM-ascending ordinals the compiled object's section indices therefore descend, and functions_occur_in_expected_order reports PARTIAL for exactly that reason -- the same state ov002/EnemySpawner+EnemySwitchTag and three other promoted entries carry. Per-function bytes are unaffected by emission order, and verify's text verdict does not gate on it.

The queue row predicted `compiler-only:>=16` from dScMgMCarlo2_c's ancestor chain (7 classes incl. self via build/rtti.json; floor 2x7+2). The measured output is recorded in verification.compilerOnlyOutput -- the compiler emits the two classes' own _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV records, the inherited vague-linkage RTTI of the dScMgSingle3DBase_c chain, and the compiler-generated D2 destructors; every one of them either has a configured ROM home (externalized after a cartridge compare) or is banked as a deadstrip policy. Nothing was widened or licensed to make the bytes reproduce.

dMgMCarlo2CardObj_c's D0 and D2 are not in the ROM: the destructor is not virtual (the vtable's two slots are Render at 0x020f98dc and Update at 0x020f9994, read out of the overlay binary), so no vtable slot can target a deleting destructor, and the cartridge carries D1 (0x020f8ff0, size 0x10) only -- the next ROM function starts at 0x020f9000, exactly D1's end, leaving no room for either variant.

No linkcheck key, by measurement rather than omission. The --partial mode was also attempted and correctly reports 0/25: with a single enrolled TU object there are no N legacy objects to substitute per-function reductions for (those shards were absorbed by the f100-bank merge, PR #2652).
